doc.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Basie's tenors and rhythm section
summary: Basie loved tenors, starting with Herschel and Lester, and had Walter Page, Jo Jones and Freddie Green.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: A question I wanted to ask you is, you know Basie has been quoted as saying that his band was developed from the rhythm section, and then up through the tenor sax positions, and then to the rest of the band.

Yeah he loved tenors. You see in those days, you only had one tenor player, featured tenor player, but he always had two so he started out with Herschel and Lester. So he had two of the world’s greatest and wasn’t nobody — he had to make it. So when they went to New York they just chopped everybody down. And that rhythm section, he had Walt Page, Jo Jones, because that was all the American rhythm section, and himself, Freddie Green. That was quite a band.
